From 9c337073d9d81a145434b22f42dc3128ecd17730 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Taniya Das <tdas@codeaurora.org>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2021 22:13:56 +0530
Subject: [PATCH] clk: qcom: gcc-sc7280: Mark gcc_cfg_noc_lpass_clk always
 enabled

The gcc cfg noc lpass clock is required to be always enabled for the
LPASS core and audio drivers to be functional.

Fixes: a3cc092196ef ("clk: qcom: Add Global Clock controller (GCC) driver for SC7280")
Signed-off-by: Taniya Das <tdas@codeaurora.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/1640018638-19436-4-git-send-email-tdas@codeaurora.org
Signed-off-by: Stephen Boyd <sboyd@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/clk/qcom/gcc-sc7280.c b/drivers/clk/qcom/gcc-sc7280.c
index 8fb6bd69f240..423627d49719 100644
--- a/drivers/clk/qcom/gcc-sc7280.c
+++ b/drivers/clk/qcom/gcc-sc7280.c
@@ -2917,7 +2917,7 @@ static struct clk_branch gcc_cfg_noc_lpass_clk = {
 		.enable_mask = BIT(0),
 		.hw.init = &(struct clk_init_data){
 			.name = "gcc_cfg_noc_lpass_clk",
-			.ops = &clk_branch2_ops,
+			.ops = &clk_branch2_aon_ops,
 		},
 	},
 };
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/clk/qcom/gcc-sc7280.c`**
   - The `ops` field of the `gcc_cfg_noc_lpass_clk` structure was changed from `&clk_branch2_ops` to `&clk_branch2_aon_ops`. This modification indicates that the clock operations for the `gcc_cfg_noc_lpass_clk` are now using a different set of operations, specifically those associated with AON (Always On) functionality.

### Relationships

- The change in the `gcc_cfg_noc_lpass_clk` structure is aimed at ensuring that the clock is always enabled for the LPASS core and audio drivers to function correctly. By switching to `&clk_branch2_aon_ops`, the patch likely enhances the reliability or functionality of the clock management for the LPASS core, addressing the underlying issue that necessitated this modification. This change is part of a broader effort to fix a bug introduced in a previous commit (identified by the hash `a3cc092196ef`).

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/1640018638-19436-4-git-send-email-tdas@codeaurora.org

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the `gcc_cfg_noc_lpass_clk` not being properly configured to always be enabled, which is essential for the LPASS core and audio drivers to function correctly. The original implementation used `&clk_branch2_ops`, which likely did not support the necessary always-on functionality, leading to potential failures in the audio subsystem when the clock was not enabled.
